claims.claim: @RuneCrypto_ posted on 2026-08-31 claiming to have acquired 37.4% of a NASDAQ-listed company for $1,800,000, describing it as a $4.8M market cap, $0.12/share stock with 92.3% short interest, $6.2M debt against $380K ARR.

The account described a plan to tokenize the stock and pair a memecoin against it so DEX volume would 'flow into the tokenized stock,' framed to trigger a squeeze given the claimed 92.3% short interest.
X's community fact-check response on the post states no NASDAQ stock matches the claimed $4.8M market cap at $0.12/share with 92.3% short interest.

The SEC approved a Nasdaq rule change (effective 2026-07-22) that places any Nasdaq-listed company with Market Value of Listed Securities below $5 million for 30 consecutive business days into immediate suspension and delisting with no standard cure period; this order was subsequently stayed pending appeal petitions as of 2026-07-29.

Nasdaq Capital Market issuers must maintain a $1.00 minimum bid price (Rule 5550(a)(2)); falling below it for 30 consecutive business days triggers a deficiency notice with cure periods historically extending up to ~540 days before delisting.

A systematic search across major short-interest screeners (highshortinterest.com, findmymoat.com, and others) found no Nasdaq-listed ticker matching the claimed combination of ~$4.8M market cap, ~$0.12 share price, and ~92.3% short interest.

FINRA's most recent short-interest-by-float ranking (data as of 2026-07-31) tops out with OSI Systems at 93.83%, followed by indie Semiconductor (86.24%), TransMedics (85.71%), Under Armour (85.21%), and Kohl's (83.24%) -- all established, liquid companies, not sub-$5M microcaps.
The claim's core figures are internally arithmetically consistent: 37.4% of a $4.8M market cap equals approximately $1,795,200, matching the stated $1.8M purchase price.

Under SEC Rule 13d-1 (amended 2023), an investor crossing 5% beneficial ownership of a public company with control intent must file an initial Schedule 13D within 5 business days; amendments to the stated plan must be disclosed within 2 business days.

Repeated SEC EDGAR full-text searches for a Schedule 13D, 13G, or 8-K filed between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-01 disclosing a new ~35-40% beneficial ownership stake for a purchase price near $1.5-2M in a small Nasdaq issuer returned no matching filing.

Every identified 2025-2026 disclosed crypto-treasury micro-cap pivot (Eightco/Worldcoin, SharpLink Gaming/Ethereum, SRM Entertainment/Tron, Sonnet BioTherapeutics/Hyperliquid) was structured as a negotiated primary-issuance PIPE or reverse merger with the acquirer named publicly the same day or within days, not silent open-market accumulation.

Eightco Holdings' pre-pivot market cap was $4.4M (about 3M shares outstanding at $1.45/share) before a $250M PIPE tied to a Worldcoin treasury strategy -- the closest real comp in size to the claimed target, and it used new-share issuance, not open-market buying.

A margin call, a securities-lending buy-in/recall notice, or a Reg SHO mandatory close-out are the mechanisms that force short covering, and all three are anchored to trades and settlement in the registered security itself, not a derivative or token that merely references its price.

GameStop's January 2021 squeeze occurred with short interest exceeding 140% of float, and the mechanical drivers (margin-forced covering, and dealer delta-hedging as options moved through strikes) both required real trades in the registered security's own order book.

The SEC's official October 2021 staff report on the GameStop episode concluded retail sentiment-driven buying, not short covering, was the primary sustained driver of the multi-week price appreciation.

Legitimate tokenized-equity issuers (Backed Finance/xStocks, Dinari dShares) back tokens 1:1 through a real creation/redemption loop: the issuer buys and custodies actual shares before minting, and burns tokens on redemption, but retail redemption is generally gated to KYC'd institutional channels with minimums around $5,000.

Every published catalog of legitimately tokenized equities (xStocks ~60-100 names, Robinhood Chain 200-2,000+ tokens, Dinari ~724 names) is composed of large, liquid, exchange-listed names -- no issuer documents support for sub-$5M-market-cap Nasdaq microcaps.

Robinhood's EU/global 'Stock Tokens' are tokenized derivative contracts issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Ltd. that track a share's price but confer no ownership, voting, or direct redemption rights -- structurally different from genuine custodial 1:1 backing -- and are not offered to US persons.

On Robinhood Chain, a memecoin called BONER paired directly against tokenized Hims & Hers (HIMS) stock absorbed roughly 53% of the tokenized HIMS float in a single pool (83% across all pools), causing the on-chain token to print $132.64 versus a real NYSE close of $28.84 -- a roughly 4.6x dislocation -- while the real exchange was closed.

Tokenized-stock daily volume on Robinhood Chain jumped from under $500K to $8.1M after Bankr/Long.xyz enabled memecoin-stock pairing in July 2026, while tokenized stocks remained only about 4% of the chain's total value locked ($12.8M of $312M).

Neither Robinhood nor the Bankr/Long.xyz memecoin-pairing layer publish an issuer-consent, minimum-market-cap, or listing-tier eligibility policy for which stocks can be tokenized or paired -- but Robinhood itself still gates which underlying stocks get tokenized at all, and its list is limited to roughly 90+ large/liquid tickers with no documented sub-$5M microcap ever added.

Architect Partners tracked 184 public companies that had disclosed plans to raise more than $132 billion for crypto-asset purchases, as of a September 2025 snapshot; a later Architect Partners report cited a different, overlapping-window figure of 221 digital-asset-treasury vehicles and ~$145B, illustrating that the headline number is a fast-moving point-in-time count, not a constant.

K33 Research found 26 of 168 tracked Bitcoin-holding public companies traded below the market value of their own crypto holdings (mNAV below 1.0x) as of mid-September 2025 -- about 15.5%, though widely mis-headlined as 'one in four' (25%); a later April 2026 analysis put the below-NAV share at roughly 40%.

CEA Industries (ticker BNC) closed at $8.88 on 2025-07-25, the last trading day before announcing a $500M PIPE-funded BNB treasury strategy backed by YZi Labs; it spiked to an intraday peak of $82.88 on announcement, then fell roughly 92% to $6.47 by December 2025 amid a PIPE-dilution selloff and an activist governance fight with YZi Labs, and traded around $3.09 by 2026-08-31 (roughly 96% below its post-announcement peak).

SEC Rule 10b-5 and Exchange Act Section 9(a)(2) require manipulative intent and an artificial-price effect, or specific intent to induce others' trading through a false appearance of activity -- publicly stating a trading thesis or announcing an acquisition is not, by itself, illegal manipulation; case law holds that aggressive trading strategies must be combined with additional deceptive conduct (false statements, wash trading, undisclosed coordinated buying) to violate these provisions.

No SEC enforcement action or criminal charge was ever brought against Keith Gill ('Roaring Kitty') personally for his GameStop-era social media activity; the only monetary penalty from that episode landed on his former employer, MML Investors Services (MassMutual), fined $4 million for supervisory failure.

The SEC's January 28, 2026 joint staff statement held that tokenizing a security does not change its legal status under federal securities law, and distinguished issuer-sponsored tokenized securities (real backing, needs issuer cooperation) from unregistered third-party synthetic tokens, which typically confer no shareholder rights and can implicate unregistered security-based-swap rules.

@RuneCrypto_ is a pseudonymous X account active since at least 2022 with roughly 164,000 followers whose established content pattern is memecoin discovery and DeFi yield-farming commentary; no public source discloses a real-world legal identity behind the handle.

$PONS is the native token of a memecoin-launchpad protocol built on Robinhood Chain (a pump.fun-style launchpad), not a bespoke memecoin created specifically to pair against the claimed NASDAQ acquisition; RuneCrypto_'s only found connection to it is routine engagement with an unrelated Hyperliquid perpetuals-listing announcement.

As of the day after the post, no coverage of the specific @RuneCrypto_ NASDAQ claim was found in mainstream crypto press (CoinDesk, The Block, Decrypt, Crypto Briefing) or on Polymarket, and no regulator has issued any statement specifically addressing the memecoin-paired-tokenized-stock mechanism as of 2026-09-01.
